Scripts you can read off the phone

Written to your register: clear plan, honest numbers, no sugarcoating. Each is one continuous take, about thirty seconds. The cover is the first frame.

Reel 01 · Same Door · ~30s

“Renting this apartment: twenty-five hundred a month. Owning the exact same apartment: twenty-five fifteen. Fifteen dollars apart, and I can say that because both listings are mine. So here’s the honest math. Twenty percent down at today’s rate, property taxes, insurance, and the association dues. All of it. Twenty-five fifteen. And about two hundred twenty of that first payment stays yours, which rent never does. Treat it as an estimate; your numbers will differ. If that gap surprised you, message me 124.”

Caption A · $2,500 to rent it. $2,515 to own it. Same apartment, both listings mine. Full math in my Same Door carousel, sources included. Estimate, not a quote. DM “124” for the breakdown.
Caption B · Fifteen dollars. That’s the real gap between renting and owning this unit, before equity. Numbers in the carousel. Send me “124” for the breakdown.
Reel 02 · The $477 · ~30s

“Four hundred seventy-seven dollars a month, and it’s nowhere on the listing. That’s the association dues on this building. It’s the number most condo buyers never check until they already love the place. Pool, spa, gym, water, trash, the building’s insurance. Skip it, and your monthly math is fiction. I read documents for a living for sixteen years before I got my license, so this is the part I never skip. Shopping for any condo, mine included: ask for the financials before you write. Message me 124 and I’ll send the exact list to ask for.”

“Снимать эту квартиру — две тысячи пятьсот в месяц. Владеть той же самой — две тысячи пятьсот пятнадцать. Разница пятнадцать долларов. Считаем честно: взнос двадцать процентов, сегодняшняя ставка, налоги, страховка, взносы ассоциации. И часть платежа остаётся вашей — аренда так не умеет. Это оценка, ваши цифры будут другими. Хотите полный расчёт по-русски — напишите мне «124».”

Before anything posts

The don’t-say list

  • Never describe a neighborhood or building by who lives there. Speaking Russian is a service you offer, never a description of an area, in either language.
  • Keep “estimate, not a quote” wherever the $2,515 appears. Rate, credit and the unit’s actual dues all move it.
  • Don’t say owning is cheaper than renting. Say “about the same before equity. Run your numbers.”
  • The $477 is the building’s recorded figure for a two-bedroom. Say “recorded for this building,” never “unit 124’s dues.”
  • No “guaranteed,” no “always appreciates,” no “can’t lose.”
  • If you boost any of it, never target by language or demographics. Housing ads follow special rules on every platform.
Two upgrades, when you’re ready

What makes this even sharper.

  • Unit 124’s own dues figure. Pull the association’s financials and the math slide gets the exact number instead of the building’s recorded one. Send it over and I’ll have the updated slide back same day.
  • Your photos of the unit. The moment you send the listing set, slide one carries the actual door instead of the Valley at dusk.

You don’t hire an agent to open the door. You hire one to read what signing it means. That’s the story this whole kit tells about you. This one’s on me. It’s the same kit I build for Jen’s listings. If it works, all I’d ask is a screenshot of the results and one sentence of feedback.
